# Results {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{r}
#| label: load-results
#| include: false

results100 <- readRDS("results/results100.rds")
effdim <- readRDS("results/effdim.rds")
summ_arith <- summarise_runs(results100, "arithmetic") |> 
  add_vrf()
summ_geo <- summarise_runs(results100, "geometric")
```
```{r}
#| label: fig-validation
#| fig-cap: 'Geometric Asian call at $d = 52$ with the sequential construction. Estimates include 95% confidence bands. Dotted: exact price.'
#| fig-scap: 'Geometric Asian call option; illustrative validation plot'
#| dev: tikz

plot_validation(summ_geo, dim = 52, cons = "Sequential")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: 'Share of the confidence intervals for the geometric call that contain the exact price, across all $d$ and both constructions.'
#| dev: tikz

coverage(summ_geo, by = "method") |> 
  kbl(
    format = "latex",
    digits = 3,
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Estimator",
      "Coverage",
      "Intervals"
    )
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 11, latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prices
#| tbl-cap: 'Asian call prices from $nM$ evaluations ($n = 2^{16}$, $M = 100$) $\pm$ the half-width 95\% confidence band. MC uses the sequential construction, RQMC the Sobol sequence with the Brownian bridge.'
#| dev: tikz

price_table(summ_arith) |> 
  kbl(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = "rrrr",
    col.names = c(
      "d",
      "Geometric (exact)",
      "Arithmetic, MC",
      "Arithmetic, RQMC"
    )
  )|> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 11, latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-convergence
#| fig-cap: 'Standard deviation (RMSE) of a single $n$-point estimate of the arithmetic call at $d=252$. Dashed: slope $- \frac12$ anchored at the MC value at $n = 2^8$.'
#| fig-scap: 'Log-log-convergence plot for arithmetic call at $d=252$'
#| dev: tikz

plot_error(summ_arith, dim = 252)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rates
#| tbl-cap: 'Empirical convergence: negative slope of a least-squares fit of $\log \hat{\sigma}_n$ on $\log n$.'
#| dev: tikz

rates_table(summ_arith) |> 
  select(- construction) |> 
  kbl(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = "lrrrrr",
    col.names = c(
      "",
      "$d = 1$",
      "$d = 4$",
      "$d = 12$",
      "$d = 52$",
      "$d = 252$"
    )
  ) |> 
  pack_rows("Sequential", 1, 4) |> 
  pack_rows("Brownian Bridge", 5,8)|> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 11, latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-vrf
#| fig-cap: "Variance reduction factor of RQMC over MC at $n = 2^{16}$ (log scales). Below the dashed line, RQMC is less efficient than MC."
#| fig-scap: 'VRFs of RQMC over MC at $n=2^{16}$'
#| dev: tikz

plot_vrf(summ_arith)
```


```{r}
#| label: tbl-vrf
#| tbl-cap: "VRFs at $n=2^{16}$, rounded to two significant digits."
#| dev: tikz

vrf_table(summ_arith) |> 
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    linesep = "",
    escape = FALSE,
    align = "llrrrrr",
    col.names = c(
      "Construction",
      "Point Set",
      "$d = 1$",
      "$d = 4$",
      "$d = 12$",
      "$d = 52$",
      "$d = 252$"
    )
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 11, latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-effdim
#| fig-cap: 'Share of the variance of the arithmetic payoff not explained by the first $s$ coordinates. The dashed line marks  the 1% level that defines the truncation dimension $d_t$.'
#| fig-scap: 'Truncation dimension and share of unexplained variance'
#| dev: tikz


plot_effective_dim(effdim)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-effdim
#| tbl-cap: 'Truncation dimension $d_t$ of the arithmetic payoff.'
#| dev: tikz

truncation_dim(effdim) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = d,
    values_from = d_t
  ) |> 
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Construction",
      "$d = 1$",
      "$d = 4$",
      "$d = 12$",
      "$d = 52$",
      "$d = 252$"
    )
  )|> 
  kable_styling(font_size = 11, latex_options = "hold_position")
```
